study.title: Somatotopic Representation of Acupoints in Human Primary Somatosensory Cortex: An fMRI Study
study.study_design: Within-subject fMRI study with block design; each subject received stimulation at all acupoints in independently randomized order
study.randomization: Order of sessions was independently randomized for each subject
study.exclusion_criteria: Subjects were screened and excluded if they had evidence or history of psychiatric and neurologic disorders

arms.arm_label_exact: Healthy volunteers receiving manual-rubbing tactile stimulation at acupoints

conditions.timepoint_exact: 30-s resting blocks; after initial resting block, resting blocks repeated 4 times
conditions.scan_context: Subjects were not stimulated throughout 30 s
Manual-rubbing tactile stimulation at acupoint LI1
Manual-rubbing tactile stimulation at acupoint SI1
Manual-rubbing tactile stimulation at acupoint LI4
Manual-rubbing tactile stimulation at acupoint LI10

Manual-rubbing tactile stimulation at acupoint LV3

interventions.stimulation_type: manual rubbing with a scrubbing sponge
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: right upper limb; on the root of the nail (finger)
interventions.manipulation_exact: A small area of skin (~4 cm2) involving each of the acupoints was repeatedly rubbed in one direction with a scrubbing sponge
interventions.session_duration_exact: 30 s per stimulation block, repeated 4 times
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: We used rubbing instead of acupuncture stimulation to raise neural activity in the level to obtain clearer fMRI data in S1 because our primary aim was to establish somatotopic mapping of the acupoints

extraction_notes.note: No coordinate tables or peak MNI coordinates are reported for any of the six acupoint activation results. Results are presented only as a brain surface figure (Fig. 1b) and a bar chart of activated voxel counts (Fig. 2). Exact coordinates cannot be extracted.

Fig. 1b shows S1 activation locations for all six acupoints on a rendered brain surface. The relative positions (lateral vs medial) are described in text and figure caption, but no numerical coordinates are provided. Cluster size values in neural results are rough visual estimates from Fig. 2 bar chart and should be treated with caution.

Fig. 2 shows the number of activated voxels per acupoint as a bar chart. No numerical values are given in the text or a table. Bar heights were visually estimated: A (LI1) ~900, B (SI1) ~50-100 (very small), C (LI4) ~500, D (LI10) ~400, E (ST36) ~500, F (LV3) ~100. These are approximations and should not be used as exact values.

No sensory or interoceptive response data (e.g., deqi, pain, sensation ratings) were collected or reported. The authors used tactile rubbing rather than acupuncture needling and did not administer any sensation questionnaire.
No expectancy, blinding, or credibility measures were assessed or reported.
No adverse events were reported. The paper does not include a statement confirming absence of adverse events.
The correction method applied at p < 0.0001 is labeled only as 'corrected' without specifying whether this is FWE, FDR, or cluster-level correction.

The paper does not report voxel size or matrix resolution in mm, only slice thickness (5 mm) and FOV (220×220 mm) with 64×64 matrix, implying in-plane resolution of ~3.4×3.4 mm but this is not explicitly stated.

The study design is within-subject (each subject received all 6 acupoint stimulations in randomized order across sessions), but the paper does not clarify whether all sessions were completed in one day or across multiple days.

The acupuncture modality was coded as 'other' because the intervention was manual tactile rubbing with a scrubbing sponge, explicitly not acupuncture needling. This differs from standard acupuncture modality classifications.
No clinical or behavioral outcome measures were assessed. This was a basic neuroscience mapping study with no patient population or therapeutic endpoints.
The FA parameter listed in the methods as 'fractional anisotropy [FA] = 909' appears to be an OCR error; it likely refers to flip angle = 90 degrees based on standard fMRI acquisition parameters.
